_readme: Machine-readable provenance manifest. Every dataset in data/raw carries an entry here stating where it came from, the period it covers, how it was retrieved, and its known limitations. The human-readable version is DATA_SOURCES.md at the repository root. Nothing in this project is used in an analysis unless it appears in this file.

datasets.title: Dubai monthly climate normals
datasets.publisher: National Center of Meteorology (NCM), UAE / Dubai Meteorological Office
datasets.period: 1977-2015 station normals, tabulated to the WMO 1991-2020 reference period
datasets.retrieval_method: Published station normals, cross-checked against the WMO tabulation
datasets.used_for: The base climate for every downstream model: thermal comfort, shade benefit, irrigation demand, solar yield.
datasets.limitations: Monthly normals, not a measured hourly time series. The 8,760-hour series used for machine learning is DOWNSCALED from these normals by a documented diurnal model (see src/climate.py) and is labelled MODELLED wherever it appears. A purchased AMY/TMY hourly file would remove this step; none was available within the competition timeframe.

datasets.title: Solar position, 8,760 hourly steps
datasets.publisher: National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL), via the pvlib-python library
datasets.citation: Reda, I. & Andreas, A. (2004, revised 2008). Solar Position Algorithm for Solar Radiation Applications. NREL/TP-560-34302.
datasets.used_for: Sun angles, shadow lengths, canopy occlusion, the annual shade-coverage model, and the solar features in the ML feature set.
datasets.limitations: None material. This is an exact astronomical calculation, not an estimate. It describes where the sun is, not how cloudy it is; cloud cover comes from the NCM sunshine-hours normals.

datasets.title: Community-level resident population
datasets.used_for: Catchment population, visitor demand model, capacity check.
datasets.limitations: Community-level totals only. The walk-ring populations are derived by applying the Al Safa area density to each ring, so they assume even distribution within the ring - reasonable for this uniformly built neighbourhood but not exact.

datasets.title: Walk-time catchment rings
datasets.limitations: Circular (as-the-crow-flies) rings, not a street-network isochrone. Real walking distance is longer than the radius; the 800 m ring is therefore a slight over-estimate of who can truly reach the park in 10 minutes.

datasets.title: Per-species irrigation demand and carbon sequestration rates
datasets.publisher: Published arid-region urban forestry literature; Ghaf figures from UAE field studies
datasets.used_for: Irrigation water balance, carbon sequestration model, planting palette selection.
datasets.limitations: Per-tree rates vary with age, soil and microclimate. Values are mid-range published figures for semi-mature specimens; the carbon model additionally applies a linear establishment curve over the first 10 years rather than crediting mature rates from year 1.

datasets._geometry_note: The X/Y bounds in this file are the AREA ACCOUNTING footprint of each zone: tight, non-overlapping rectangles that sum exactly to the 15,000 m2 site. They are not the drawn shape. The spine and its two planted margins are built on a meandering centreline (src/config.py SPINE.curve_amplitude_m), and the shade model, the planting layout and the drawn plans all use that curve. Rectangle areas and curve areas agree (140 m x 6 m walkway, 140 m x 5 m each margin); only the outline differs.
datasets.title: Masterplan zoning schedule with geometry
datasets.used_for: Area schedule, cost take-off, and the spatial grid used by the per-square-metre comfort model.
datasets.limitations: Zone rectangles are the design's own geometry. The 150x100 m site envelope is an ASSUMPTION pending confirmation against the supplied DWG file - every area figure depends on it.

datasets.title: Dubai construction and utility unit rates
datasets.publisher: Dubai landscape contractor quotations; DEWA published tariff schedule
datasets.used_for: Capital cost estimate, operations and maintenance model, 30-year life-cycle cost.
datasets.limitations: Rates are the upper bound of quoted ranges, which is deliberately conservative. A real tender would price lower or higher depending on market conditions at the time.

datasets.title: Competition brief, Neighbourhood Parks Manual, site DWG, master plan
datasets.used_for: Brief compliance, capacity benchmarks (150-400 users per 10,000 sqm), design standards, site boundary.
datasets.limitations: The DWG has not yet been opened and dimensioned; see site_zoning_schedule.csv limitation.

integrity_rules: Every figure in every report traces to a file in data/raw or to a documented computation over one.
Any series that is modelled rather than measured is labelled MODELLED at the point of use, not only here.
Where a source has a known weakness it is stated in this file and repeated in DATA_SOURCES.md. Nothing is quietly smoothed over.
No dataset is generated to make a result look better. Where the data is weak the conclusion is stated as weak.
